modelResponse.episodeSummary: 72F, severe bradycardia, critical hemodynamic instability (BP 72/44), shock.
keyECGEvidence: atropine 1 mg x2 with no heart response
modelResponse.mechanism: Depression of the sinoatrial node and conduction system due to elevated extracellular potassium, leading to junctional escape and bradycardia.
contributingFactors: Acute Kidney Injury (Creatinine 3.2 mg/dL CRITICAL HIGH)

rejectedAlternatives.why: No digoxin listed in home or active medications; no mention of digitalis use in history.
No thyroid function data provided; clinical presentation is more consistent with acute renal failure/hyperkalemia.

recommendedActions: Administer intravenous Calcium Gluconate or Calcium Chloride to stabilize cardiac membranes
Administer IV insulin with glucose (Dextrose) to shift potassium intracellularly
Administer inhaled Albuterol (high dose) to shift potassium intracellularly
Initiate urgent hemodialysis given AKI and symptomatic hyperkalemia
Continue IV fluids cautiously while monitoring for volume overload
Withhold Lisinopril (ACE inhibitor) due to AKI and hyperkalemia
uncertainty: The degree of bradycardia (32 bpm) and lack of atropine response is more severe than the K+ 6.4 mmol/L would typically suggest, though hyperkalemia remains the most likely driver.
